newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends up on cattle expectations, weather.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends up on cattle expectations, weather.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed higher on prospects for a large cattle placements figure in Friday's USDA seven state cattle-on-feed report, traders said.

An average of analysts' estimates pegged the U.S. cattle placements tally for April at 13.9 percent above a year ago. USDA released the report at 1400 CDT and showed the placements tally at 12 percent above a year ago in the seven key states.
Corn also found support from a cold snap overnight Thursday that led to some concern that portions of the U.S. crop may have been damaged.
But that scenario was not a dramatic one.
Meteorologists said emerged corn may have sustained minor damage from the cold spell.

"There's a little bit of cold weather to it and some talk of business showing up but nothing dramatic," said Jack Scoville, Vice President for Price Futures Group. "Also it held some support levels and some shorts were getting out with a nice profit."
The short covering followed a price slide this week but traders said key support levels held.
Corn closed 3/4 to 3-1/2 cents per bushel higher, with July up 2-3/4 at $2.84-1/2.
Slow farmer selling and firm cash basis markets also buoyed the nearby corn futures contracts.
"It's getting hard to buy corn in the cash markets in the country," said Charlie Sernatinger, analyst with E.D. and F. Man International.

In spread trading FIMAT Futures did one milion bushels of September/July at 14-1/4 cents, premium July, LFG Futures spread one million July/September at 14-3/4 cents, premium July and Iowa Grain spread one million July/December at 18 cents, premium July, traders said.
Lee B. Stern and Co bought six million bushels of July and FIMAT Futures sold seven million bushels of December, traders said.
Corn futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 48,000 contracts, above the 43,490 traded Thursday.

In corn options, Goldenberg Hehmeyer bought 1,500 December $3.00 calls at eight to 8-1/8 cents, FIMAT Futures bought 500 July $2.70 puts at 2-3/8 cents and sold 500 July $2.60 puts at 7/8 cent, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 10,000 contracts, above the 8,833 traded Thursday.
